analysis:
No concrete regression found in the visible changes.

Handshake (CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift:136-149): a 30s default deadline now bounds TCP/TLS/WS upgrade to .ready. PendingHandshake.take() under an NSLock gives the continuation to exactly one of the state handler or the deadline, so there is no double resume. The deadline path clears the handler and cancels the connection. Transport selection by URL scheme (connectionParameters, lines 55-61) is unchanged in behavior: wss/https gets TLS and everything else is plaintext. That is the existing ws:// test path; nothing here adds a downgrade. Registration (auth token, attestation) is still sent only after .ready (line 153), so TB-002 sequencing is preserved. A hung handshake no longer strands the reconnect loop, which is a small availability gain. Minor: the continuation is not cancellation-aware, so shutdown during a handshake can wait up to 30s. This is not a security issue.

Terminal states (terminalState init, lines 55-64): .waiting is treated as terminal during and after the handshake. The head comments suggest the post-ready behavior already existed, so this is not new. The effect is faster reconnects with backoff.

Config: handshakeTimeout is public and defaults to 30. A caller-supplied value of zero or a negative number would only produce immediate failure, which is an availability matter and outside the threat model.

Drain (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift:103-119): the outcome can now be .drained without a coordinator acknowledgement when hasRegisteredConnection() is false. The reasoning is that a disconnect already cancelled accepted work. Open integration questions: (1) sessionRegistered is set only after sendRegistration (Connection.swift:153-159), so a registration frame may already have reached the coordinator while hasRegisteredConnection() still reports false. (2) Whether the reconnect loop is stopped or the provider re-registers after a drained outcome is not visible in this batch. If either holds, the coordinator could route work to a provider that has declared itself drained, which would matter for logout, update and credential-revocation sequencing (A-008, A-016, T-053). The hasRegisteredConnection() implementation and the shutdownRequested and drain interplay need review in the unchanged files. I could not confirm or exclude that window from the supplied evidence, so I recorded it as an open question rather than a finding.
